Replay

Resuming a saved party

4 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
LifecycleRecovery semanticsAcceptance and remaining work

Room_Options.restore_published lets a fresh Room recover a durable checkpoint when its previous authority is gone. Party enables this for trusted hosting members (excluding observers). A live authority always takes precedence: Room joins that host normally. Existing live migration and frozen-owner recovery keep their own paths.

Odin
options.restore_published = true
// WSS by default; explicit loopback WS is available for local development.
options.checkpoint_local_development = local_development
error := replaygd.room_open(&room, initial_frame, game_model, options)
// Continue the usual frame loop. No separate download or restore pump is needed.
error = replaygd.room_frame(&room, delta_seconds, controls)

The initial frame is used only for a genuinely new bootstrap room. It is never substituted for missing, corrupt, disallowed or too-old saved progress.

Lifecycle#

After fresh process registration and an authenticated view with no live authority, Room computes the schema and configuration needed to validate the saved state without creating a simulation timeline. It reads publication status, downloads the selected revision, decodes the complete typed checkpoint and verifies the stable token's playable reservation. Dedicated authority uses local seat zero.

Room validates and installs packaged dependencies into checkpoint_cache before requesting authority. Room owns the prepared checkpoint independently of transfer buffers. The existing preparation_ready callback must approve referenced assets before Room requests authority. While waiting, ordinary authority queries continue and the completed download's ACK can retry, releasing the service transfer slot. If another host becomes live, Room releases its pending recovery state and joins it instead.

The explicit Restore request shares the authority Lease's request sequence; Room does not start another RPC while it is pending. A successful correlated grant is required, followed by a fresh successful renewal before session_resume starts a runtime. This prevents validation/transfer latency from consuming most of the lease before expensive runtime setup. The runtime uses the saved configuration/state, correct local seat and freshly registered incarnation under the newer epoch. There is no uncoordinated authority fallback.

A Restore reply may arrive after its conservative local deadline: that deadline is anchored to request start, while the coordinator granted ownership later. Room retains the exact prepared point and requests renewal when the authenticated view still reports this actor's reservation. It does not request another Restore or install a runtime using the expired permit. A successful correlated renewal can make the same epoch usable. If the coordinator has also expired or replaced the reservation, renewal is refused and normal recovery/join rules apply.

Retrying a request does not override the service's policy decision. Busy during status/download means another bounded transfer is in progress; Room retries a new status request after backoff instead of showing a terminal recovery error. Busy on an authority request retains the prepared bytes for a later new attempt. Stale publication/transport timeout returns to status lookup. Connection/generation changes preserve owned bytes while the control context is refreshed. An exact already-granted Point with a live authenticated lease can still be installed after a lost reply. A stale local permit needs fresh authorization; an expired coordinator reservation needs a new recovery grant.

Room.restore.phase exposes Checking, Downloading, Preparing, Requesting, Granted, Complete or Failed. error and authority_error preserve storage/protocol and authority-policy detail. Missing saves, unsupported contracts, denied reservations and excessive rollback remain visible failures. room_restore_retry permits an explicit retry for a fresh Room without an initialized Session. Cavecrawl displays progress and a retry button through its existing party menu.

Recovery semantics#

The normal checkpoint resume policy retires pending accepted actions explicitly and disconnects nonlocal saved peers until they reconnect. Stable tokens, reserved seats and action frontiers survive. A game's normal leave/join rules apply to those peers; Room does not invent an alternate inventory policy. The restoring local player keeps its saved state. Personal profile persistence remains separate.

Room.recovery.from_publication identifies this path. checkpoint_tick is the restored boundary and service_known_tick is the latest authenticated pre-attempt authority tick observed by this Room. known_lost_ticks uses that known tick; previous_confirmed stays zero because a fresh process had no local timeline. This is a known rollback distance from that view, not proof about unreported work or every earlier grant lost across service restarts. Installation/interruption timing remains available through the existing recovery metrics.

Acceptance and remaining work#

Cavecrawl's Rejoin recent party resumes stored progress after the original game process exits and the service is killed/restarted. Native verified-TLS and fresh-browser/RTC tests restore the exact saved tick with three gems in epoch 2, accept a new guest and its loot action, then publish the continued game again. The browser test uses explicit loopback development WS. Separate database readers validate the final saved inventories. The original live handoff/rejoin gate still passes with publication enabled.

Competing-return fixtures retain the same published checkpoint in two fresh registered processes before releasing their recovery attempts. One becomes the new authority; the other observes that live host and joins it. Native release-order tests cover both possible owner seats and verify one epoch advance plus conserved loot in the next durable publication. A browser RTC race exercises the same transition. Temporary Busy responses must not strand a participant before it can reach that transition.

The tested recovery path covers Cavecrawl under these conditions. Bounded atomic asset packages also support Scrapyard sprays and native/browser restoration with an empty asset cache. Broader asset profiles, acceptance of other games' UI/state, public deployment, and broader recovery/failure policies remain outside this coverage. See the guarded service decision.
